Location: Welshpool, Western Australia 6106
Employment Type: Full-Time
Salary: $100,000 – $130,000 per annum (depending on skills and experience)

MINPROVISE INTERNATIONAL PTY LTD is a leading total solutions provider delivering specialist maintenance and shutdown services, engineering, fabrication, project services, and sustaining capital works. We also provide a comprehensive range of equipment and products, supporting the mining, oil & gas, and construction industries across Australia and internationally.

We are currently seeking an experienced and motivated Safety Advisor / Occupational Health and Safety Advisor to join our growing team on a full-time basis.

About the Role
As a Safety Advisor / Occupational Health and Safety Advisor, you will be responsible for supporting the implementation, monitoring, and continuous improvement of workplace health and safety systems across mining, engineering, maintenance, fabrication, and industrial projects. You will work closely with project managers, supervisors, employees, and contractors to ensure compliance with legislation, company policies, and client safety requirements.

Key Responsibilities
•	Implement, maintain, and monitor workplace health and safety systems, policies, and procedures.
•	Provide advice and guidance to management, supervisors, and employees on occupational health and safety matters.
•	Conduct workplace inspections, audits, risk assessments, and safety observations.
•	Identify workplace hazards and recommend appropriate control measures to minimise risks.
•	Assist with incident investigations, reporting, root cause analysis, and corrective actions.
•	Develop, review, and maintain safety documentation, including SWMS, JSA, risk assessments, and safety reports.
•	Monitor compliance with WHS legislation, Australian Standards, client requirements, and company procedures.
•	Deliver safety inductions, toolbox talks, and training sessions to employees and contractors.
•	Promote a strong safety culture and encourage continuous improvement in workplace practices.
•	Assist project teams with safety planning, mobilisation requirements, and compliance documentation.
•	Maintain safety records, registers, inspection reports, and incident databases.
•	Liaise with clients, contractors, and regulatory bodies regarding health and safety matters where required.
•	Ensure compliance with workplace health, safety, environmental, and quality management systems.

Skills and Experience
•	Minimum 1-2 years of full-time experience as a Safety Advisor, Occupational Health and Safety Advisor, or similar WHS role.
•	Relevant qualification in Occupational Health and Safety, Workplace Health and Safety, or a related discipline.
•	Strong knowledge of Australian WHS legislation, safety management systems, and risk management principles.
•	Experience working within mining, construction, engineering, maintenance, or industrial environments is highly regarded.
•	Ability to conduct workplace inspections, audits, investigations, and safety training.
•	Strong communication, consultation, and problem-solving skills.
•	Excellent attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities.
•	Ability to work independently and collaboratively with project teams.
•	Proficiency in Microsoft Office and safety management systems.

What We Offer
•	Full-time, permanent employment.
•	Competitive salary of $100,000 – $130,000 per annum.
•	Opportunities to work on major mining, shutdown, engineering, and industrial projects.
•	Ongoing professional development and career progression.
•	Supportive team environment with long-term career opportunities.

MINPROVISE INTERNATIONAL PTY LTD is a leading total solutions provider delivering specialist maintenance and shutdown services, engineering, fabrication, project services, and sustaining capital works. We also provide a comprehensive range of equipment and products, supporting the mining, oil & gas, and construction industries across Australia and internationally.

We are currently seeking experienced and motivated Riggers to join our growing team on a full-time basis.

About the Role
As a Rigger, you will be responsible for planning, preparing, and performing rigging operations to safely lift, move, position, and secure heavy machinery, structural steel, equipment, and materials across mining, oil & gas, construction, and industrial projects. You will work closely with crane operators, engineers, supervisors, and other trades to ensure lifting activities are carried out safely and efficiently in accordance with Australian Standards and site requirements.

Key Responsibilities
•	Read and interpret lifting plans, engineering drawings, and work instructions.
•	Plan and perform rigging operations for lifting, positioning, and installation of heavy equipment and structural components.
•	Select, inspect, and safely use lifting gear, including slings, chains, wire ropes, shackles, spreader bars, lifting beams, and hoists.
•	Direct crane operators using standard hand signals and radio communications during lifting operations.
•	Assemble, dismantle, align, and secure heavy machinery, plant, structural steel, and industrial equipment.
•	Conduct pre-start inspections of rigging equipment and ensure all lifting gear is certified and fit for use.
•	Identify hazards, assess lifting risks, and implement appropriate control measures.
•	Assist with shutdowns, maintenance projects, equipment installations, and major construction activities.
•	Maintain accurate records of lifting equipment inspections and completed work where required.
•	Work collaboratively with supervisors, engineers, crane operators, and other trades to ensure projects are completed safely and on schedule.
•	Follow all workplace health and safety policies, procedures, and environmental requirements.

Skills and Experience
•	Minimum 1–2 years of full-time experience as a Rigger in mining, construction, or heavy industrial environments.
•	Current High Risk Work Licence – Rigging (Basic, Intermediate, or Advanced).
•	Strong knowledge of lifting techniques, rigging equipment, and safe lifting practices.
•	Ability to read and interpret lifting plans, engineering drawings, and technical specifications.
•	Experience working with cranes, heavy equipment, structural steel, and mechanical installations.
•	Strong commitment to workplace safety and compliance with Australian Standards.
•	Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
•	Excellent communication, problem-solving, and organisational skills.

What We Offer

•	Opportunities to work on major mining, shutdown, and industrial projects.
•	Ongoing training and career development.

REQ675207 - St George Hospital - Clinical Nurse Consultant 2 - Apheresis - Temporary Full Time

The Role 

The vision for South Eastern Sydney Local Health District (SESLHD) is 'exceptional care, healthier lives'. SESLHD is committed to enabling our community to be healthy and well, and to providing the best possible compassionate care when people need it. 
The Clinical Nurse Consultant is a Registered Nurse who has responsibility for ensuring the safe and timely provision of apheresis services at St George Hospital.

Benefits
 

Up to 12 allocated days off each year (for full-time employees) in addition to annual leave.

Salary packaging optionsthat reduce your taxable income and increase your take-home pay! Up to $9K for living expenses and $2.6K meal & entertainment & Novated Leasing.

Discounted gym memberships with a Fitness Passport.

Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for employees and family members.

Discounted Private Health Insurance.

Selection Criteria

Current Authority to Practice as a Registered Nurse-Midwife, Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia and current NSW Drivers License (if required by service).

Minimum five years full time equivalent post qualification experience, with at least three years full time equivalent experience in the specialty field and post graduate qualifications relevant to the field of practice.

Demonstrated effective communication and inter-personal skills across a variety of mediums and an understanding of the practice development framework.

Proven ability to implement changes and develop direction in clinical practice by the utilisation of evidence based research.

Demonstrated skills in strategic and clinical service planning including an understanding of organisational behaviour, change management and cultural change processes.

Demonstrated skills in clinical teaching, competency in the use of contemporary information systems and experience in the development of specialty education programs.

Demonstrated clinical expertise in client-centred consultancy with the ability to work independently.

Accreditation and competence in all apheresis related procedures including stem cell collection.

REQ676281 - St George Hospital - Clinical Nurse Consultant 2 - 6D Orthopaedics - Permanent Full Time

The Role 

The vision for South Eastern Sydney Local Health District (SESLHD) is 'exceptional care, healthier lives'. SESLHD is committed to enabling our community to be healthy and well, and to providing the best possible compassionate care when people need it. 

All staff are expected to act as an appropriate and effective role model and promote culture and supporting practices that reflect the NSW Health CORE values of Collaboration, Openness, Respect and Empowerment through demonstrated behaviours and interactions with patients, clients and employees. All staff are expected to take reasonable care that their actions do not adversely affect the health and safety of others, that they comply with any reasonable instruction that is given them and with any reasonable policies-procedures relating to health or safety in the workplace, as well as notifying any hazards-risks or incidents to their managers. 

The vision for nursing and midwifery at St George Hospital is to provide meaning and purpose to plan for the future;have reference to an inspirational statement that is consistent with the purpose and values of nursing and midwifery;and to inspire nurses and midwives to provide the highest quality healthcare to patients in any circumstance. The Vision Statement is:'Nurses and midwives at St George Hospital are always compassionate and competent in the delivery of excellent patient and family centred care.' Eight core behaviours were identified as being integral to achieving the vision:team player;caring;respectful;honest;advocate;collaborative;considerate and accountable. 

Clinical Nurse Consultant Grade 2 means:a registered nurse appointed as such to a position approved by the Health Service, who has at least 5 years full time equivalent post registration experience, with at least 3 years full time equivalent experience in the specialty field. In addition the employee must have approved post graduate nursing qualifications relevant to the field in which he-she is appointed to or such other qualifications or experience deemed appropriate by the Health Service. An employer may also require a higher qualification in the specialist nursing field where such qualification is considered essential for the performance of the individual position. 

Benefits
 

Up to 12 allocated days off each year (for full-time employees) in addition to annual leave.

Salary packaging optionsthat reduce your taxable income and increase your take-home pay! Up to $9K for living expenses and $2.6K meal & entertainment & Novated Leasing.

Discounted gym memberships with a Fitness Passport.

Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for employees and family members.

Discounted Private Health Insurance.

Selection Criteria

Current Authority to Practice as a Registered Nurse, Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia and current NSW Driver's License (if required by service).

Minimum five years full time equivalent post qualification experience, with at least three years full time equivalent experience in the specialty field in an acute care facility and-or post graduate qualifications relevant to the field of practice.

Demonstrated effective communication and inter-personal skills across a variety of mediums and an understanding of the practice development framework.

Proven ability to implement changes and develop direction in clinical practice by the utilisation of evidence based research.

Demonstrated skills in strategic and clinical service planning including an understanding of organisational behaviour, change management and cultural change processes.

Demonstrated skills in clinical teaching, competency in the use of contemporary information systems and experience in the development of specialty education programs.

Demonstrated clinical expertise in client-centered consultancy with the ability to work independently.
